title: Residency exceptions and oncall playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc is a pragmatic playbook for handling exceptions to region pinning and other data-residency constraints in Private deployments. It’s intended for SREs, on-call engs, solutions engineers, and compliance reviewers. Focus is operational: how to detect, decide, act, and record when pinned-region constraints collide with infra failures, migrations, or customer requests.

Status & usage notes:
- Living doc (work-in-progress). Pull into incident runbook when residency constraints are implicated.
- Assumes the platform exposes a region_pin metadata field for deployments and a hard/soft enforcement mode.
- Where contract language or customer agreements explicitly prohibit fallback, follow legal/CS guidance and escalate to Product + Legal.

Common scenarios covered:
1) Region unreachable (zone or region outage) and requests are blocked by strict pin
2) Customer requests temporary cross-region failover for SLA preservation (exception request)
3) Migration windows where data must be moved across regions (planned exceptions)
4) Operator error created wrong pin at creation time (configuration exception)

Quick decision matrix (summary):
- If enforcement_mode == "hard" AND contract_requires_locality == true -> NO automated failover. Trigger incident and notify CS/Legal.
- If enforcement_mode == "soft" OR contract_allows_fallback -> Apply pre-approved fallback policy (see fallback table) and open exception ticket.
- For planned migrations -> use Migration Flow A (below) with documented consent and retention policy updates.

Fallback table (examples):
- Primary: eu-west-1 (hard pin) -> Fallback: none (deny) if contract strict
- Primary: eu-west-1 (soft pin) -> Fallback: eu-central-1 with data-in-transit TLS, KV-cache flush on return
- Primary: ap-southeast-2 -> Fallback: ap-northeast-1 only during business-hours maintenance (notify customer)

Operational run steps (incident):
1) Detect: alert from routing service that region X is degraded; error rate spike on pinned routes listed in monitoring dashboard.
2) Triage: Confirm pinned-region value in deployment metadata. Check enforcement mode.
3) Quick legal check: If contract tag contains "sovereign" OR "no-fallback", ping CS + Legal channel (Slack: #legal-compliance) with incident ID.
4) If allowed by policy, flip route policy to fallback variant (API call: POST /internal/routing/override {deployment, fallback_region, reason, expires_at}). Use CLI helper: rdwctl residency override.
5) Invalidate any local-only caches (prefix cache, KV entries with locality markers). Record cache flush steps in ticket.
6) Enable additional logging: set debug-residency=true for affected deployment for 4 hours.
7) Customer comms: use template in appendix; route through CS.
8) Post-incident: revert override, validate data locality (consistency checks), and create RCA with residency-specific items.

Planned migration flow (Migration Flow A):
- Preconditions: written customer consent recorded; migration window agreed; KMS keys available in target region or cross-region wrap allowed; compliance checklist signed off.
- Steps: create target VPC and storage, snapshot, initiate transfer via secure transfer agent, perform hash checks, spin up canary in target region with read-only pin, run consistency tests, cutover read-write with dual-write grace period, update deployment pin, revoke temporary cross-region keys, record GRC artifacts.
- Post-migration: run data locality audit, update invoices (if pricing differs), and log the event in the customer ledger.

Escalation & on-call responsibilities:
- Pager owner (SRE oncall): lead detection/triage and initial override decisions within policy bounds.
- Platform lead: approve any cross-region fallback beyond emergency threshold ( > 30 minutes or data-sensitive customer).
- Compliance lead / Legal: must sign off if enforcement_mode is hard or if contract clauses apply.

Audit & documentation checklist (for every exception):
- Ticket created in Jira with prefix RES-
- Owner assigned and time-stamped decisions
- Reason for exception and fallbacks tried
- List of affected deployments and customer IDs
- Copies of communication to customers + timestamps
- Data movement logs and cryptographic checksums
- KMS / key access logs for temporary keys
- Post-incident RCA with timelines and remediation actions

Telemetry and monitoring additions (must be present):
- Residency-violation metric: counter of requests blocked due to pin
- Residency-fallback metric: counter of successful fallback activations
- Per-deployment residency_state tag in traces
- Automated audit report generated weekly for pinned deployments (csv)

Templates (snippets)
- Slack ping to CS/Legal: "INCIDENT RES-<id> region pin conflict: deployment <d-id> pinned to <region>. Enforcement=<hard|soft>. Impact=<brief>. Need legal input re: fallback. Owner: <oncall>."
- Customer high-level note (CS template): "We observed degraded connectivity to the region you requested. To keep your service available we temporarily routed traffic to <fallback-region> on <date/time>. No persistent data will remain in the fallback region after failback. If you prefer we can keep the hard pin and accept degraded availability — let us know."

Examples & edge cases observed in runbook history:
- Case 2024-07-21: EU customer with soft pin allowed fallback; fallback succeeded but cache invalidation missed a prefix; resulted in 3 stale reads. Remediation: added cache-prefetch verification step.
- Case 2024-09-03: Operator accidentally created deployment with wrong pin (US instead of EU). Quick fix: rollback created resources and create new deployment; but we lacked fast data wipe automation — manual wipe took 6 hours. Action: add automated destroy-and-wipe in provisioning.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Improper overrides create unauthorized cross-border copies. Mitigation: temporary overrides must be time-limited and audited; auto-expire enforcement is required.
- Risk: Customer confusion about where data lived during incident. Mitigation: CS templates + mandatory post-incident reconciliation call for any fallback > 1 hour.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who signs off for non-customer-initiated cross-region fallbacks for enterprise customers? (Product, Legal, or CTO?)
- Automation: build rdwctl residency-rollback action that also validates cache and KMS state — owned by infra team.
- Data retention policy during emergency fallbacks needs product + legal harmonization (duration, delete guarantees).

Appendix: quick commands and links
- CLI overrides: rdwctl residency override --deployment <id> --fallback <region> --expires <ISO> --reason "Incident RES-<id>"
- Revert: rdwctl residency revert --deployment <id>
- Debug logs: links to per-deployment logging dashboard (confluence id: CONFLUENCE-1234)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally prescriptive: we want oncalls to have a clear set of allowed actions. Please comment with any legal constraints I’ve missed or customer contract language that would change the decision tree.
- If you are a solutions engineer, add common customer-approved fallback patterns you use in sales conversations so they can be codified.
